title: Proof of x^2 + y^2 >= 2xy with Equality Characterization
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Prove that x^2 + y^2 >= 2xy holds for all real numbers x and y, and show that equality occurs if and only if x = y.

steps.title: Move Everything to One Side
steps.explanation: Subtracting 2xy from both sides is an equivalence-preserving operation that recasts the claim as nonnegativity of a single expression.
steps.why: Adding or subtracting the same real number from an inequality never changes its truth value.

steps.title: Recognize the Perfect Square
steps.explanation: The leftover trinomial is exactly the expansion of (x - y)^2, so the inequality reduces to the statement that a square is nonnegative.
steps.why: Binomial expansion (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2 matches the trinomial term by term with a = x, b = y.

steps.title: Invoke Nonnegativity of Squares
steps.explanation: Whatever real value x - y takes, its square is nonnegative, so the transformed inequality is unconditionally true, proving the original.
steps.why: In an ordered field, t^2 >= 0 always: t and t have the same sign, and the product of same-signed numbers is nonnegative.

steps.title: Characterize the Equality Case
steps.explanation: A square of a real number vanishes only when the number itself is zero, so equality in the original inequality pins down x = y exactly.
steps.why: The reals have no nonzero nilpotents: t^2 = 0 forces t = 0, giving a biconditional rather than a one-way implication.
